summary: Orbital Command is an interactive web game where students design, launch and run a complete space mission. Players choose one of five missions: Moon, Mars, Europa, Earth observation or an asteroid. They then build a spacecraft, add science instruments, pick a rocket and plan the orbit. A live engineering engine checks mass, power, cost, signal strength, rocket capacity and trajectory, and shows green, yellow or red results. A mission cannot launch until critical problems are fixed, and the game explains how to fix them. The player then flies a nine-phase simulation with events that depend on the design, and receives a report with a score out of 100. It solves the Space Mission Design Game challenge by turning real engineering trade-offs into something students can try and replay. It matters because it makes space engineering simple, fun and open to everyone.
details:
What it does and how it works

Orbital Command is a game where you build and fly your own space mission.

  1. Pick a mission: Moon, Mars, Europa, Earth observation or an asteroid.
  2. Build your spacecraft and add science tools.
  3. Choose a rocket and plan the path in space.
  4. The game checks your design with green, yellow or red signs.
  5. If something is red, you cannot launch. The game tells you how to fix it.
  6. Fly the mission and make choices when problems come up.
  7. At the end, you get a score out of 100 and tips to do better.

Benefits

  • You learn by playing, not just by reading.
  • You see how weight, power and money affect a space mission.
  • It has quizzes, points and badges to keep you interested.
  • It works on phone and computer, with nothing to install.

Intended impact

We want more students to understand how space missions work and feel excited about space and science. Teachers can also use it in class.

Tools we used

React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, Framer Motion and Recharts. The website is hosted on Netlify. We also used AI (Claude by Anthropic) to help with code and the presentation, and our team checked the results.

How it is creative

  • It is a real game, not just a website with facts.
  • A bad design cannot launch, so every mistake teaches something.
  • The mission events depend on your own design, so every player has a different story.
  • It looks like a real mission control room, but the words are easy to understand.

What our team considered

  • Easy words and clear steps for beginners.
  • Simple, reasonable science. The numbers are estimates, not official NASA data.
  • Fair results, so players know why they won or lost.
  • Works on all devices, with no login.
  • Replay, badges and five missions, so students keep practicing.
